## layout-preview

```text
Propose an auto-layout for one diagram and write it as a proposal JSON file

Usage: processcraft-cli layout-preview [OPTIONS] --document-id <DOCUMENT_ID> --diagram-id <DIAGRAM_ID> --out <OUT> <INPUT>

Arguments:
  <INPUT>  Input .processcraft project

Options:
      --document-id <DOCUMENT_ID>
          Document ID (listed by `info`)
      --diagram-id <DIAGRAM_ID>
          Diagram ID within the document (listed by `info`)
      --choreography-scope-shape <CHOREOGRAPHY_SCOPE_SHAPE>
          Lay out the direct children of this expanded SubChoreography representation
      --out <OUT>
          Proposal JSON file to write
      --overwrite
          
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## layout-apply

```text
Apply a layout proposal to its project and save the result to a new file

Usage: processcraft-cli layout-apply [OPTIONS] --proposal <PROPOSAL> --out <OUT> <INPUT>

Arguments:
  <INPUT>  Input .processcraft project

Options:
      --proposal <PROPOSAL>  Proposal JSON written by layout-preview
      --out <OUT>            New .processcraft file to write
      --overwrite            
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## export-image

```text
Render one diagram to SVG, PNG or PDF

Usage: processcraft-cli export-image [OPTIONS] --document-id <DOCUMENT_ID> --diagram-id <DIAGRAM_ID> --format <FORMAT> --out <OUT> <INPUT>

Arguments:
  <INPUT>  Input .processcraft project

Options:
      --document-id <DOCUMENT_ID>
          Document ID (listed by `info`)
      --diagram-id <DIAGRAM_ID>
          Diagram ID within the document (listed by `info`)
      --format <FORMAT>
          Image format [possible values: svg, png, pdf]
      --out <OUT>
          Image file to write
      --scale <SCALE>
          Scale factor within 0.125..8 [default: 1]
      --dark
          Render with the dark appearance
      --overwrite
          Replace the output file if it exists
      --acknowledge-diagnostics
          Export even when the render preflight reports diagnostics
      --overlay-attribute <OVERLAY_ATTRIBUTE>
          Attribute definition ID to draw as an overlay with a legend (see `query attributes`)
      --overlay-mode <OVERLAY_MODE>
          Overlay style: a five-step heatmap (default) or value badges [possible values: heatmap, badge]
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## import-bpmn

```text
Import BPMN 2.0 XML into a new .processcraft project (editable when it fits the qualified profile)

Usage: processcraft-cli import-bpmn [OPTIONS] --out <OUT> <INPUT>

Arguments:
  <INPUT>  BPMN XML file

Options:
      --out <OUT>  .processcraft file to write
      --overwrite  Replace the output file if it exists
  -h, --help       Print help
```

## export-bpmn

```text
Export one document of a project as BPMN 2.0 XML

Usage: processcraft-cli export-bpmn [OPTIONS] --document-id <DOCUMENT_ID> --out <OUT> <INPUT>

Arguments:
  <INPUT>  Input .processcraft project

Options:
      --document-id <DOCUMENT_ID>  Document ID (listed by `info`)
      --out <OUT>                  BPMN XML file to write
      --overwrite                  Replace the output file if it exists
      --acknowledge-native-fields  Export even though native-only project links are omitted
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

## export-drawio

```text
Export one diagram as an uncompressed draw.io file using draw.io's BPMN shapes

Usage: processcraft-cli export-drawio [OPTIONS] --document-id <DOCUMENT_ID> --diagram-id <DIAGRAM_ID> --out <OUT> <INPUT>

Arguments:
  <INPUT>  Input .processcraft project

Options:
      --document-id <DOCUMENT_ID>  Document ID (listed by `info`)
      --diagram-id <DIAGRAM_ID>    Diagram ID within the document (listed by `info`)
      --out <OUT>                  .drawio file to write
      --overwrite                  Replace the output file if it exists
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

## export-raci

```text
Export the RACI matrix of one process as CSV (UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF)

Usage: processcraft-cli export-raci [OPTIONS] --out <OUT> <INPUT> <DOCUMENT_ID> <PROCESS_ID>

Arguments:
  <INPUT>        Input .processcraft project
  <DOCUMENT_ID>  Document ID (listed by `info`)
  <PROCESS_ID>   Process ID within the document

Options:
      --out <OUT>  .csv file to write
      --overwrite  Replace the output file if it exists
  -h, --help       Print help
```

## mcp

```text
Serve the Model Context Protocol over stdio, standalone or attached to the GUI

Usage: processcraft-cli mcp [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --new <NEW>                 Start from a new, unsaved project with this name
      --in <INPUT>                Open this .processcraft project
      --attach <ATTACH>           Attach to the GUI session published on this named pipe
      --token <TOKEN>             Attachment token shown by the GUI
      --session <SESSION>         GUI session ID to attach to
      --read-root <READ_ROOTS>    Folder MCP file tools may read from (repeatable)
      --write-root <WRITE_ROOTS>  Folder MCP file tools may write to (repeatable)
  -h, --help                      Print help
```

## query

```text
Read project projections as JSON without modifying the file

Usage: processcraft-cli query <PATH> <COMMAND>

Commands:
  model               Read every modeled document field, including ordered XML and common metadata
  checkpoint-fields   Read detailed checkpoint differences as bounded JSON Pointer pages
  events              Read event roots, references, flags and owned data as bounded field pages
  diagrams            Read DI attributes and representation endpoints as bounded field pages
  identities          Read persistent semantic/DI selectors and their optional XML IDs
  data                Read scoped data declarations, ports and associations as bounded field pages
  catalog             Read supporting catalog values as bounded JSON Pointer pages
  comments            
  checkpoints         
  compare-checkpoint  
  library             
  dictionary          
  documents           Documents with their ids, capability and processes (id, name, lanes)
  conventions         The stored conventions profile, or null
  usages              
  table               
  raci                RACI matrix of one process: role columns, activity rows, R/A/C/I cells
  diagnostics         Diagnostics of the stored conventions profile (built-in checks when none is stored)
  attributes          Read custom attribute definitions and per-element values of one document
  replace-options     List the BPMN types an element or sequence flow can be replaced with (replaceElement targets)
  help                Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  <PATH>  Input .processcraft project

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## validate

```text
Validate a project, or the prepared import of a BPMN file

Usage: processcraft-cli validate [OPTIONS] <PATH>

Arguments:
  <PATH>  .processcraft project or BPMN XML file

Options:
      --json               Emit JSON (always the output format)
      --profile <FILE>     Evaluate this conventions profile (JSON, same schema as setConventionsProfile) instead of the stored one
      --fail-on <FAIL_ON>  Severity that makes validate exit 3; errors always do [default: error] [possible values: error, warning]
  -h, --help               Print help
```

## run

```text
Apply a command batch to a new or existing project and save it to --out.

Besides the primitive mutations, a batch can use the compound modeling commands that the GUI and MCP share: connect, append, createAt, moveElements, resizeShape, reconnect, replaceElement, addLane, splitLane, createPool, toggleCollapse, makeSpace, align (`shape_ids`, `alignment`: left|center|right|top|middle|bottom), distribute (`shape_ids`, `distribution`: horizontal|vertical), and duplicate (`element_ids`, `dx`, `dy`, optional `target_diagram_id`; copy and paste with fresh IDs). The whole batch is one undo step. `commands --json` lists every command with its parameters.

Usage: processcraft-cli run [OPTIONS] --batch <BATCH> --out <OUT>

Options:
      --new <NAME>
          Start from a new project with this name

      --in <INPUT>
          Start from this .processcraft project

      --batch <BATCH>
          JSON batch request file (schema: `commands --json`)

      --out <OUT>
          .processcraft file to write

      --overwrite
          Replace an existing output file other than the input

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
